source_name: NOAA daily weather for Seattle, 2012 to 2015 (public domain), via vega-datasets
how_read: Taken once by tools/snapshot_tables.py from the vega_datasets package; kept the date, rain in mm, and the day's highest and lowest temperature in degrees C.
note: The vega_datasets package describes the file as drawn from public-domain NOAA data (https://www.weather.gov/disclaimer).

source_name: US Bureau of Transportation Statistics on-time data, January to March 2001 (a 20,000-flight sample), via vega-datasets
how_read: Taken once by tools/snapshot_tables.py from the vega_datasets package; kept departure time, origin, destination, distance in miles and arrival delay in minutes (negative means early).
note: US government statistics. The 20,000 flights are the sample published in the vega-datasets collection, not the full record.

source_name: Robert Shiller's long-run U.S. stock data (S&P 500 monthly average price, CPI), via the open datasets project
how_read: Downloaded once by tools/snapshot_tables.py; kept the months from December 1949 to December 2022, which are Shiller's own series (the project extends it with FRED prices after mid-2023). Prices are monthly averages.
note: The project releases its compiled csv under the ODC Public Domain Dedication and License, says there is no exact licence statement for the original data, and suggests crediting Robert Shiller.

source_name: Our World in Data: life expectancy at birth (Riley; Zijdeman et al.; Human Mortality Database; UN World Population Prospects)
how_read: Downloaded once as a csv by tools/snapshot_tables.py; kept every fifth year from 1990 to 2020. A year a country has no figure for is simply absent.
note: Our World in Data's own processing is licensed CC BY, and the numbers come from the providers named here: credit both Our World in Data and the provider. Countries with at least 2 million people in 2020 only.

source_name: Documented base rates: each fact names its own source page, the day it was read and the words or table row that show the number
how_read: Each page was read in full on the day shown. Numbers are copied as printed; a threshold is only used when it sits clear of the documented value and of the rounding the source used.
note: Claims about a range of cohorts use the lowest and highest cohort values seen on the page.
